item.description:
The Padma Barrage project is expected to be inaugurated in February 2027, according to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Water Resources.
The committee expressed the expectation at its second meeting at the National Parliament on Wednesday, chaired by its chairman, Mohammad Shofiqul Haque Milon, MP.
The meeting also discussed the national interests involved in the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty with India. It noted that no final decision has been made on whether to continue the existing treaty or renew it, although the process remains underway.
The committee discussed a planned visit to Sujanagar upazila in Pabnadistrict on October 25 as part of its assessment of the Padma Barrage project.
At the outset, the committee confirmed the minutes of its first meeting, subject to corrections. It then reviewed the implementation progress of two projects approved at the previous meeting: erosion control along the Brahmaputra and Jinjiram rivers in Jamalpur district, and riverbank protection along the left bank of the Jamuna, the Old Brahmaputra and the Alai rivers flowing through the district, said a press release of parliament secretariat.
The meeting also received reports on the Barnoi River re-excavation, pollution removal and encroachment prevention project in Rajshahi and Natore districts; the second revised rehabilitation project for polder systems along the Naf River in Ukhiya and Teknaf upazilas of Cox's Bazar to improve Bangladesh-Myanmar border security; and emergency maintenance and rehabilitation works under the Ganges-Kobadak Irrigation Project.
The committee reviewed the implementation progress of these projects in detail.
Committee members, including Water Resources Minister Md Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee, MP, and State Minister Forhad Hossain Azad, MP, attended the meeting.
Other participants included A E Sultan Mahmud Babu, Mohammad Mazharul Islam, Md Faridul Kabir Talukder, Md Izzatullah, Md Oli Ullah and Md Moshiur Rahman Khan.
The water resources secretary, director generals of various agencies under the ministry, heads of relevant organizations and boards, senior officials and officials of the National Parliament Secretariat also attended the meeting.

item.title: Home minister: No plan for an operation like ‘Clean Heart’
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has said the government has no plans at present to launch an operation similar to "Operation Clean Heart".
He made the statement while speaking to journalists after inaugurating the Criminal Investigation Department’s (CID) Cyber Police Centre at Dampara Police Lines in Chittagong on Wednesday afternoon.
The minister said crime patterns had changed over time, with digital platforms and cyberspace increasingly being used to commit various offences, including fraud and stock market manipulation.
“There is no alternative to modern digital forensic laboratories to prevent and investigate these crimes,” he said, adding that the government had taken an initiative to establish digital forensic laboratories at all eight divisional headquarters as soon as possible.
Salahuddin Ahmed said the South Korean government and the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) had provided assistance in establishing the CID’s cyber office and digital forensic laboratory in Chittagong.
He thanked the South Korean government, the country’s ambassador to Bangladesh, KOICA representatives and members of the visiting Korean team for their support.
The minister said the government had been planning to establish a police cyber unit from the outset. The unit formally began operations on October 1 under the leadership of an additional inspector general of police.
The newly inaugurated digital forensic laboratory will operate under the CID’s leadership. However, interdepartmental cooperation among the relevant units will continue in conducting digital forensic analysis and examinations, he added.
He further said the government planned to expand digital analysis capabilities at the central, divisional, district and upazila levels. To this end, initiatives would be taken to establish laboratory facilities at divisional and district levels.
The government had sought international cooperation for the initiative, including assistance from South Korea, the minister said.
Referring to the CID’s existing facilities, Salahuddin Ahmed said the department had operated chemical laboratories since its establishment. These laboratories play an important role in various examinations, including the preparation of viscera reports.
He said expanding the laboratories had become necessary to meet current needs. Proper analysis, evidence and certification are essential to speeding up judicial proceedings and ensuring that people receive justice, he added.
The minister also stressed the need to modernize law enforcement agencies in response to changing crime patterns. The government was taking steps to equip them with the necessary laboratory facilities, logistical support and modern equipment to prevent and investigate crimes committed in the digital sphere.
Responding to a question about the overall law and order situation, Salahuddin Ahmed said the government had a responsibility to address it but did not consider the situation a challenge.
“The government has responsibilities in all areas, and the necessary measures will be taken to fulfil them,” he said.
Asked about attacks on police during operations to arrest suspects, the minister said police officers were sometimes attacked by criminals, but such incidents were not new.
He said police were making every effort to combat crime and added that appropriate legal action would be taken against anyone found to have obstructed police from arresting a suspect or assisted a suspect, provided specific information supported such allegations.
Chittagong-10 MP Saeed Al Noman, South Korean Ambassador to Bangladesh Kim Ji-jun, Inspector General of Police Ali Hossain Fakir, CID Additional Inspector General Barrister Mohammad Mosharraf Hossain and other police officials were present at the event.

item.title: Rabiul: Govt committed to enacting comprehensive road safety law by 2027
item.description:
Road Transport and Bridges, Railways and Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam on Wednesday said the government is firmly committed to enacting a comprehensive road safety law by 2027.
"The government was taking swift initiatives to ensure road safety. Various measures are also being taken, including updating helmet standards, enforcing speed limits, strengthening post-crash medical care, constructing underpasses, building left-side lanes on highways and improving road safety data management," he said.
He made the remarks while addressing a roundtable discussion marking National Road Safety Day 2026 at a hotel in the capital.
BRAC's Road Safety Program and Road Safety Coalition Bangladesh jointly organized the discussion titled "Government Commitment to Improving Road Safety in Bangladesh".
Rabiul said the government, the World Bank and various other organizations were working to ensure road safety. However, despite the collective efforts, the desired progress had not been achieved. A lack of coordinated initiatives and insufficient awareness about personal safety were making the situation more complicated, he added.
He said road safety programs should not be limited to a particular day; effective initiatives must be taken throughout the year. To halve road crash fatalities by 2030, the government, non-governmental organizations, development partners, transport owners' and workers' associations, and all other relevant stakeholders must work together, he added.
This year's National Road Safety Day theme is "Safe Roads, Prosperous Country, Bangladesh First".
The roundtable, organized under this theme, discussed the country's road safety situation, the government's national and international commitments, recent progress and future actions.
Particular emphasis was placed on implementing the Safe System Approach to reduce road crash deaths and serious injuries.
The minister said the government was taking various measures to improve road safety. In line with national and global commitments, initiatives were being taken to update helmet standards, enforce speed limits and formulate the necessary guidelines. At the same time, ensuring prompt medical treatment after crashes and strengthening emergency services to save injured people's lives were also receiving priority, he added.
He said projects were being undertaken to improve infrastructure safety through the construction of underpasses and the development of left-side lanes on highways.
The government was also working to ensure safe road crossings for school and college students and improve the recording and management of road crash data. Greater coordination among the relevant agencies was needed to implement these initiatives, he added.
Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Labour and Employment Shamsur Rahman Shimul Biswas, MP, Secretary of the Road Transport and Highways Division Dr Mohammad Ziaul Haque, and Secretary of the Ministry of Textiles and Jute Sharaf Uddin Ahmed Chowdhury attended the roundtable as special guests.
Speaking as a special guest, Shamsur Rahman Shimul Biswas said extensive changes to Bangladesh's existing road management system had become essential. People were suffering constantly because of unsafe road management.
Although different parties were blaming one another for the situation, collective initiatives were needed to find a lasting solution, he added.
He said the prime minister was working with the highest priority on bringing changes to the road transport sector. Efforts were also underway to dismantle the existing mafia system in the sector, he added.
At the beginning of the program, Ahmed Najmul Hussain, director of BRAC's Road Safety Program, delivered the welcome and introductory remarks.
Later, M Khalid Mahmud, program manager of the same program, made a PowerPoint presentation highlighting Bangladesh's road safety situation, the government's commitments, recent progress and policy priorities, including the enactment of a road safety law.
During the open discussion, participants exchanged views on enacting a comprehensive road safety law, effectively enforcing existing laws and regulations, and reducing road crash deaths and serious injuries.

item.title: Bangladesh workers’ charter seeks COP31 voice, fair climate compensation
item.description:
Bangladesh’s workers have called for greater representation in international climate negotiations, fair compensation for climate-related losses and stronger safeguards for their livelihoods ahead of the UN climate conference COP31.
The Bangladesh Workers’ Charter for COP31, unveiled in Dhaka on Wednesday by the National Alliance for Just Transition Bangladesh (NAJTB), in collaboration with Manusher Jonno Foundation (MJF) and Bangladesh Labour Foundation (BLF), outlines 23 demands across eight negotiation tracks.
The charter highlights the growing threats posed by extreme heat, climate-induced displacement and industrial decarbonisation, particularly to informal workers, women and communities dependent on climate-sensitive sectors.
Speakers at the event urged the government to include workers, especially women, in Bangladesh’s official COP31 delegation and ensure that the transition to a greener economy does not undermine workers’ rights, wages or job security.
Syed Sultan Uddin Ahmmed, executive coordinator of NAJTB and executive director of the Bangladesh Institute of Labour Studies (BILS), said workers made significant contributions to the national economy but bore the consequences of a climate crisis they had done little to cause.
Rejecting debt-based climate finance and charity-driven approaches, he called for compensation commensurate with actual losses and meaningful worker participation in decisions affecting their jobs and livelihoods.
Shaheen Anam, executive director of MJF, said informal workers, who account for approximately 84% of Bangladesh’s workforce, faced disproportionate risks from climate change.
She called for income protection, job security, decent working conditions and targeted support for women, who often shoulder additional unpaid care responsibilities while facing the risk of technological displacement.
Anam also urged the government to include a woman worker in Bangladesh’s COP31 delegation, referring to the prime minister’s instruction to ensure worker representation.
AKM Ashraf Uddin, member secretary of NAJTB and executive director of BLF, said a green transition would not be sustainable if workers lost their jobs, wages and opportunities to participate in climate negotiations.
He called on the government, the International Labour Organization (ILO) and international development partners to ensure that workers’ concerns were reflected in COP31 discussions.
Presenting the keynote paper, Mir Mohammad Ali, assistant professor at Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University, outlined the growing impact of climate change on employment and livelihoods.
Citing World Bank estimates, he said Bangladesh lost approximately 250 million workdays to heat-related illness in 2024, highlighting the economic toll of rising temperatures and unsafe working conditions.
The charter was developed through eight consultations involving 43 organisations. It calls for stronger social protection, safer workplaces, greater worker participation in climate policymaking and adequately funded programmes to retrain workers affected by the shift to a low-carbon economy.
Anowar Hossen, chief coordinator of NAJTB, called for collective action to address climate-related loss and damage and protect workers in vulnerable communities.
Addressing the event, Shaikh Faridul Islam, state minister for environment, forest and climate change, described the charter as timely and comprehensive.
He said the ministry would make every effort to incorporate relevant demands into national and local climate policies, as well as Bangladesh’s position paper for COP31.
The state minister also said the government had initiated measures to generate 4,000 megawatts of solar power within three months, including 296MW in Dhaka district, highlighting the potential of renewable energy development to create jobs.
However, speakers stressed that expanding renewable energy alone would not ensure a just transition without adequate worker protection, training and opportunities to participate in the emerging green economy.
A panel discussion moderated by Shaheen Anam featured Dr Mohammad Emran Hasan, head of climate justice and natural resource rights at Oxfam in Bangladesh; Md Shamsul Islam, deputy secretary at the Ministry of Labour and Employment; Mir Mohammad Ali; and Rajekuzzaman Ratan of the Socialist Workers Front (SSF), who also coordinates NAJTB.
The panellists highlighted unequal access to climate finance, occupational exposure to extreme heat, technological displacement and gaps in labour protection.
They called for grant-based climate finance, evidence-based compensation for climate-related losses and greater inclusion of women and informal workers in climate policymaking.
Shakil Akhter Choudhury, NAJTB coordinator and representative of Sramik Karmachari Oikya Parishad (SKOP), presented the charter, which sets out workers’ priorities across eight negotiation tracks ahead of COP31.
The demands seek to place workers’ rights and livelihoods at the centre of climate action, including decisions on adaptation, loss and damage, climate finance and the transition away from carbon-intensive industries.
The charter’s central message is that workers must not be left to bear the economic and social costs of climate policies without adequate support or a meaningful role in shaping them.
Among those attending the event were Max Tunon, ILO country director in Bangladesh; Amer Salim, chairman of the Standing Committee on Just Transition at the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA); Md Shamsul Islam of the Ministry of Labour and Employment; and Zubaer Alam, programme officer at BLF.
As Bangladesh prepares for COP31, the charter calls for a negotiated just transition that recognises workers not merely as victims of climate change but as essential stakeholders in decisions affecting employment, workplace safety and future livelihoods.

item.title: FIFA to offer members $6.35-billion development fund windfall
item.description:
Football's world governing body FIFA is planning to set up a $6.35-billion development fund for the next four years, AFP learned Wednesday from a source close to the matter.
The plan is due to be approved at its Council meeting on Thursday in Zurich, where FIFA president Gianni Infantino and the 36 other members of the federation's executive will gather.
To finance this development fund for the 2026-2030 period, which would allow money to be distributed to FIFA's 211 federations as well as to the regional confederations, it would draw in part on its financial reserves after a commercially triumphant 2026 World Cup.
The plan, first revealed by the Associated Press, would allow for the payment of $25 million to each of its 211 member federations.
This is far more than the $10 million called for by two of Infantino's chief critics, Aleksander Ceferin, the boss of the European confederation UEFA, and Victor Montagliani, the head of CONCACAF, the confederation of North and Central America and the Caribbean.
Thursday's gathering is the first such meeting since April 28, and comes amid a crisis in the governance of world football, following Infantino's announcement this summer of his desire to open FIFA's premium competitions such as the World to private investors.
That plan was ultimately abandoned in the face of widespread criticism from the football world, with a rebellion led by UEFA, CONCACAF, and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC).
At the end of September, Infantino launched a consultation process with the federations to reform how the global body operates, announcing that the first proposals could be examined as early as Thursday's Council meeting.
The 56-year-old, who has headed FIFA since 2016, is running for re-election in March 2027.
His opponents have so far failed to agree on a candidate.
Ceferin has chosen to stand for a new term at the helm of UEFA and, according to several media outlets, Montagliani is expected to do the same at CONCACAF.
The deadline for submitting candidacies is November 18.

item.title: Load-shedding worsens in 21 southwestern districts, deficit hits 116MW
item.description:
Load-shedding has intensified across 21 districts in southwestern Bangladesh, including Khulna, with the power deficit reaching 116 megawatts (MW) during peak hours on Wednesday evening.
The shortage stood at 101MW during the afternoon, leaving residents grappling with frequent and prolonged power cuts.
Belal Hossain, a resident of Goborchaka in Khulna, told Dhaka Tribune that the situation had deteriorated compared with Tuesday.
“Previously, we experienced power cuts for an hour at a time. On Wednesday, outages lasted up to one and a half hours at a stretch. We are now facing 13–14 hours of load-shedding a day,” he said.
Ambia Khatun, a resident of Boyra, said frequent power cuts had compounded the hardship caused by the ongoing gas shortage.
“Gas supply is already severely disrupted, and we are trying to cope by using electricity. Frequent load-shedding has made the situation even more unbearable,” she said.
Latika Rani of Tutpara also reported a sudden deterioration in the power supply, saying outages often occurred even when electricity was urgently needed.
According to the central control room of the West Zone Power Distribution Company Ltd (WZPDCL), electricity demand across its 21-district service area stood at 694MW on Wednesday evening, against a supply of 578MW, leaving a deficit of 116MW.
In the Khulna zone, demand was 528MW, while supply stood at 447MW, resulting in a shortfall of 81MW. In the Barisal zone, demand was 166MW against a supply of 131MW, leaving a deficit of 35MW.
District-wise figures showed load-shedding of 29MW in Khulna, 4MW in Magura, 3MW in Narail, 11MW in Jhenaidah, 2MW in Chuadanga, 1MW in Meherpur, 12MW in Faridpur, 13MW in Rajbari, 4MW in Madaripur, 1MW each in Gopalganj and Shariatpur, 22MW in Barisal, 2MW each in Pirojpur and Jhalakathi, 3MW in Patuakhali, 2MW in Barguna and 4MW in Bhola.
At around 1:00pm on Wednesday, demand across the 21 districts stood at 661MW, while supply was 560MW, leaving a shortfall of 101MW.
In the Khulna zone, demand was 481MW against a supply of 422MW, resulting in a deficit of 59MW. In the Barisal zone, demand stood at 180MW, while supply was 138MW, leaving a shortfall of 42MW. Afternoon figures showed load-shedding of 17MW in Khulna, 6MW in Magura, 1MW in Narail, 7MW in Jhenaidah, 1MW in Bheramara, 7MW in Kushtia, 10MW in Rajbari, 5MW in Madaripur, 3MW in Gopalganj, 2MW in Shariatpur, 25MW in Barisal, 3MW each in Pirojpur and Jhalakathi, 5MW in Patuakhali, and 3MW each in Barguna and Bhola.
The situation was comparatively better on Tuesday, October 13. At 1:00pm, demand across the 21 districts stood at 741MW against a supply of 705MW, leaving a deficit of 36MW. In the Khulna zone, demand was 567MW and supply 531MW, while the Barisal zone met its full demand of 174MW.
By 7:00pm, the overall deficit had risen to 79MW, with demand at 721MW and supply at 642MW. In the Khulna zone, demand stood at 551MW against a supply of 504MW, leaving a shortfall of 47MW. In the Barisal zone, demand was 170MW, while supply stood at 138MW, resulting in a deficit of 32MW.

Bangladesh failed to vaccinate children, independent review finds
item.description:
A joint independent review team has identified gaps in childhood immunisation, depleted stocks of measles-rubella vaccines in 2025 and delays in a special vaccination campaign as reasons for the measles outbreak in Bangladesh.

The team of international and local experts also said the incumbent government’s response to the outbreak was inadequate. It found that Bangladesh had failed to vaccinate children.

The experts warned that outbreaks of other diseases, including whooping cough and diphtheria, could occur unless urgent action was taken. They recommended addressing shortcomings in local vaccination planning, filling vacant positions in the workforce and ensuring an uninterrupted supply of vaccines.

The findings were presented at a hotel in the capital on Wednesday. A Joint Independent Review Team comprising representatives of the World Health Organization (WHO), UNICEF, Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, officials from the Ministry of Health and the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI), and public health experts investigated and assessed various aspects of the measles outbreak, the vaccination situation and EPI activities.

The team said it would be difficult for Bangladesh to maintain its achievements and reputation in vaccination. The measles outbreak was a clear warning, it added.

The review involved international and local experts organised into nine subteams, including one national team and eight divisional teams. Each divisional team collected information from two upazilas in two districts.

The teams gathered data by visiting vaccination centres, interviewing mothers who had left vaccination centres without vaccinating their children, speaking to 10 new mothers in each area, visiting schools and madrasahs, and interviewing mothers and daughters in five households.

The 70-member team began its work on 3 October.

Wednesday’s event was primarily a workshop. Katrina Kretsinger, head of the Joint Independent Review Team, presented the main findings of the investigation and assessment. The public health expert has worked for more than 20 years with the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the WHO. Representatives of the eight divisional teams also delivered separate presentations.

At the event, Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Hossain said it was necessary to verify the quality of the vaccines administered to children.

He said the entire cold chain needed to be examined, from where vaccines were manufactured and which warehouses received them to the flights and airports through which they were transported, how they were moved from ports to district level, and how they reached vaccination centres.

Addressing the international representatives present, he said, “We assume that the vaccines are of good quality. That is an assumption. But I urge you to verify their quality as well.”

Causes of the measles outbreak

In the main presentation, Katrina Kretsinger outlined the history of Bangladesh’s EPI programme and described the vaccines administered to prevent various diseases. Explaining the causes of the measles outbreak, she said most of those infected had not been vaccinated.

The independent review found that children had been left unvaccinated both during the Awami League government’s tenure and under the previous interim government.

Kretsinger said an immunity gap had developed among children before the outbreak. Under routine immunisation programmes, around 20 per cent of children are left unvaccinated each year, with some variation.

Between 2000 and 2025, a total of 849,619 children missed measles vaccination. Stocks of measles-rubella vaccines ran out in 2025.

Her presentation showed that the most recent measles-rubella vaccination campaign had been conducted in 2020. The next campaign was due in 2024 but was postponed. A decision was taken to hold it in 2025, but it did not take place that year. A typhoid vaccination campaign was conducted in 2025, while the measles-rubella campaign was eventually held in April 2026. The delay in the measles-rubella campaign was one of the reasons behind the outbreak, she said.

Kretsinger identified several other contributing factors, including Bangladesh’s high population density and social gatherings. Vaccination is administered to children aged nine months and older, but children younger than nine months are also contracting measles.

The independent review team also assessed the current government’s response to the outbreak. It concluded that the response had been inadequate and delayed. The government had not extended vaccination to everyone at risk, including children older than five years.

The presentation also appeared to indirectly question the government’s figures for patients presenting with measles symptoms and those confirmed to have the disease.

As of 12 October, samples from 93,852 people who sought treatment with measles symptoms had been tested. Measles was detected in 68,867 of them, meaning 73 per cent of those tested were positive.

The government’s figures show a much lower proportion. According to a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) press release on Wednesday, 208,570 suspected measles patients had been admitted to hospitals across the country so far, of whom 22,840 were confirmed to have the disease. Confirmed cases accounted for 11 per cent of suspected cases.

Where the weaknesses lie

The independent review team said the measles outbreak was a warning that the population’s immunity was weakening. It described the outbreak as a test for the country and warned that, without urgent action, outbreaks of whooping cough and diphtheria would be only a matter of time. Polio could also re-emerge, it said.

The team’s presentation identified local vaccination planning as a major weakness in Bangladesh. It said the shortcomings meant that 15 to 20 per cent of children were systematically being left out of immunisation.
Vaccination workers have to administer vaccines while also maintaining records and providing counselling.

Nutrition has not received sufficient attention in vaccination programmes, the presentation said. There is also limited preparedness to deal with problems or adverse events during vaccination.

The review team said the EPI faced a significant shortage of personnel. Around 53 per cent of technician posts responsible for maintaining the cold chain were vacant, as were 34 per cent of field-level health assistant and health inspector posts. In addition, 45 per cent of positions at the EPI’s central office were vacant.

In urban areas, 90 per cent of vaccination workers were employed by non-governmental organisations, and oversight of their work was very weak, the team said.

Vaccination activities were also disrupted for seven months in 2025 because of work stoppages by vaccination workers.

What needs to be done

Local vaccination plans must be redesigned, extending down to the ward level. Vacant positions at different levels need to be filled quickly. The age limit for vaccination should be expanded, and an uninterrupted vaccine supply must be ensured. The team also recommended promptly finalising a plan for vaccine procurement after Gavi’s support ends.

Other recommendations included better coordination among organisations supporting vaccination and greater attention to urban areas. The team also proposed introducing a system to check whether children have received all required vaccines before they enrol in school.

Addressing civil surgeons from different districts who attended the event, Prime Minister’s Special Assistant SM Zia Uddin Haider said they were well aware of the problems. If civil surgeons ensured that vaccination activities were properly conducted in their respective districts, many of the problems could be resolved, he said.

Representatives of several international organisations expressed concern over the current measles situation in Bangladesh.

Gavi representative Dierk Geyl said many people in urban areas remained outside the vaccination system, often without being noticed. Vaccination efforts in cities needed to be strengthened, he added.

UNICEF’s acting representative in Dhaka, Gillian Mellsop, said the measles outbreak in 2026 was unfortunate despite Bangladesh’s strong history of vaccination. She recommended introducing a digital system to track who was receiving vaccines.

WHO Representative to Bangladesh Rajesh Narwal said Bangladesh’s vaccination system had been recognised as strong for decades. Its foundation remained solid, but modernising the system was essential.

103 Saudi-bound flights from Bangladesh disrupted, affecting 15,779 passengers
item.description:
Disruptions at various airports in Saudi Arabia have affected 103 flights operating between Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia on direct and transit routes. Some of the flights have been cancelled, while others have been suspended.

A total of 15,779 passengers on these flights have been affected.

The Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) disclosed the information in a press release issued at 2:00pm today, Thursday.

According to CAAB, 42 of the 103 flights were direct flights and 61 were transit flights.

Among the direct flights, 17 belonged to Biman Bangladesh Airlines, 10 to US-Bangla Airlines, eight to Saudia Airlines and seven to Riyadh Air.

Among the transit flights, 22 belonged to IndiGo, 14 to Emirates, seven to SalamAir, eight to Qatar Airways, six to flydubai, three to Air India and one to EgyptAir.

Until Wednesday, 100 flights had been affected, involving 15,393 passengers. The latest CAAB figures show an increase in both the number of disrupted flights and affected passengers.

Amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, Yemen's Houthi rebels have launched repeated attacks on Saudi Arabia. The deadliest attack took place last Saturday.

A total of 14 people, including two Bangladeshis, were killed in the attacks, while many others were injured. Following the attacks, flights from Dhaka to Saudi Arabia began facing disruptions.

Bangladeshi passengers travelling to Saudi Arabia have been facing difficulties as a result. Some passengers are trying to reach Saudi Arabia by taking flights to alternative destinations.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines initially suspended its Riyadh-bound flights and later suspended flights to Dammam. The state-owned carrier has announced that all flights from Dhaka to Riyadh and Dammam will remain suspended until 17 October in the interest of passenger safety.

Meanwhile, private airline US-Bangla Airlines has cancelled its Riyadh-bound flights until 21 October.

item.title: School roof collapse kills teacher, 27 children in Pakistan
item.description:
PAKISTAN-ACCIDENT-SCHOOL

Twenty-seven pupils and a teacher were killed on Thursday after a roof collapsed at a school in the northwest Pakistani city of Peshawar, a hospital official said.

Asim Khan from Peshawar''s Lady Reading Hospital confirmed the toll to AFP, adding that over 30 people were injured, with six believed to be in a critical condition.

A spokesman for the emergency rescue service in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province said the schoolchildren were crushed and trapped after the roof gave way.

"When the Rescue 1122 emergency response teams arrived at the scene, they found that one roof had collapsed on to another, causing the classroom below to be crushed and trapping children inside," spokesman Bilal Ahmad Faizi said.

"There are concerns that more children may still be trapped beneath the rubble," he said, adding that 16 ambulances, two disaster response vehicles and more than 60 personnel were deployed to the site.

Images released by the emergency services showed rescue workers in high-vis vests scrambling to move debris, rubble and dirt.

AFP journalists saw dozens of people at the scene.

Resident Sher Ahmed said he blamed "substandard construction materials" for the tragedy, and called for a probe.

"With profound grief and sorrow, I urge the authorities to conduct a thorough investigation and take strict action against anyone found responsible so that such tragedies can be prevented in the future," he said.

''Deep sorrow''

Pakistan''s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in a statement expressed "deep sorrow and grief over the loss of precious lives".

"The Prime Minister extends his condolences to the bereaved families and prays for them to have the strength and patience to bear this irreparable loss," the statement said.

President Asif Ali Zardari branded the roof collapse a "heartbreaking tragedy".

"In this hour of grief, the entire nation shares the sorrow of the affected families," he said in a statement.

Roof and building collapses are common across Pakistan, mainly because of poor safety standards and shoddy construction materials in the South Asian nation of more than 240 million people.

In June this year more than a dozen children were killed in a roof collapse at a tutoring centre in the eastern city of Lahore.

In 2025, 27 people were killed and 10 injured when a five-storey building collapsed in the impoverished area of Lyari in the southern city of Karachi.

item.description:
Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended all flights from Dhaka to Dammam and Riyadh until Sunday (Bangladesh Standard Time) following ongoing security concerns and attacks on Saudi Arabian airports.
The Public Relations Department of Biman Bangladesh Airlines disclosed the information on Thursday afternoon, citing passenger safety concerns. Updated schedules and further decisions regarding the suspended flights will be communicated in due course.
To accommodate affected travelers, Biman informed that passengers can still fly to and from Saudi Arabia using the Jeddah and Medina international airports.
To address the surge in passenger demand, Biman has deployed a larger Boeing 777 aircraft on the Medina route in place of the Boeing 787, adding 148 seats per flight. Additionally, three extra flights have been scheduled on the Jeddah route.
Passengers have been advised to contact their nearest Biman Bangladesh Airlines sales center for ticketing and travel updates.

item.title: Solar projects could save Tk754 crore over 20 years, assessment finds
item.description:
Bangladesh could save an estimated Tk753.75 crore over 20 years by installing solar power systems at public universities, National University-affiliated colleges and selected urban areas, according to an assessment presented in Dhaka on Thursday.
The proposed installations would have a combined capacity of 132.61 megawatt-peak (MWp) and require an estimated initial investment of Tk731 crore. They would cover 31 public universities, 150 colleges affiliated with the National University, Shailkupa municipality and Rajshahi city.
The assessment was presented at a citizen dialogue organized by the Consumers Association of Bangladesh (CAB) at the Dhaka Reporters Unity auditorium on October 15.
The proposed systems are estimated to generate 192.7 million units of electricity in the first year and around 3.7 billion units over 20 years. The assessment estimates that electricity could be generated at around Tk4 per unit, depending on the project and installation type.
The assessment identifies 52.50MWp of potential solar capacity across 31 public universities, requiring an estimated investment of Tk288 crore.
For 150 National University-affiliated colleges, it identifies a further 51.12MWp of capacity, with projected annual generation exceeding 71.4 million units of electricity.
The estimated levelized cost of electricity is Tk4.04 per unit for the university projects and Tk4.15 per unit for the college projects.
The assessment also examines installations in Shailkupa municipality and Rajshahi city. Shailkupa has an estimated potential of 4.36MWp through rooftop, ground-mounted and floating solar installations, while the potential identified for Rajshahi is 24.63MWp.
The estimated cost of electricity is Tk4 per unit for Shailkupa and Tk4.04 per unit for Rajshahi. Electricity generated through floating solar installations in Shailkupa is estimated to cost Tk4.75 per unit.
Together, the proposed installations across the universities, colleges and the two urban areas would bring the estimated capacity to 132.61MWp.
The estimates are based on site assessments, electricity-generation simulations and financial calculations. Actual generation and costs could vary depending on operating conditions, maintenance, financing arrangements and grid connectivity.
The assessment estimates that the proposed projects could generate Tk2,777 crore in electricity sales over 20 years, assuming a benchmark selling price of Tk7.50 per unit.
The projected sales revenue should not be treated as net profit, as operating expenses, financing costs, taxes, insurance and equipment replacement would have to be deducted.
The estimated savings of Tk753.75 crore are based on a comparison between an assumed alternative electricity-generation cost of Tk10 per unit and a solar electricity purchase price of Tk7.50 per unit. This produces an estimated difference of Tk2.50 per unit.
The assessment's savings estimate depends on the projected generation and the assumptions used in the financial calculations. Actual savings would depend on which sources of electricity solar power replaces and which costs can be avoided.
Power Division Secretary Mirana Mahrook, the chief guest at the dialogue, said the government was expanding solar power initiatives and had considered proposals from stakeholders.
She said the government had taken initiatives, including measures to reduce import duties, and would consider further proposals to support solar power development.
On the benchmark price for merchant power, Mahrook said Tk7.50 per unit was reasonable under current conditions. She added that the price could decline as incentives and facilities improved.
The proposed projects would allow institutions and urban areas to generate electricity through solar installations, but their financial viability would depend on the cost of equipment, long-term maintenance and arrangements for purchasing the electricity produced.
CAB energy adviser M Shamsul Alam said rooftop solar electricity could cost around Tk4.50 per unit. He said solar power could reduce dependence on fuel purchases and protect consumers from volatility in international fuel markets.
Alam also emphasized the importance of energy conservation. However, he questioned whether government agencies had sufficient capacity to maintain solar installations under the capital expenditure (capex) model.
Omera LPG Chief Executive Officer Masudur Rahim identified maintenance, equipment security and payment guarantees as barriers to investment.
He raised concerns about investor security when solar installations are placed on buildings owned by others. The theft of electrical transformers and cables was another concern, while delayed payments or unpaid electricity bills could undermine investors' ability to recover their costs.
Other entrepreneurs at the dialogue also stressed the need for reliable payment arrangements, transparent contracts and clearly defined maintenance responsibilities.
These concerns highlight the importance of establishing clear agreements among investors, electricity purchasers and the institutions hosting solar installations before projects begin operating.
The assessment indicates that technical potential and projected costs alone will not determine whether the installations succeed. Financing, secure equipment, dependable payments and clearly assigned operational responsibilities will also affect long-term performance.
The proposed installations are estimated to avoid around 2.3 million tons of carbon dioxide emissions over 20 years, based on an emissions factor of 0.62 tons per megawatt-hour.
The actual reduction would depend on the sources of electricity displaced by solar generation and the composition of the electricity grid's generation mix over the projects' operating lives.
Long-term performance would also depend on maintenance, grid connections, transparent procurement processes and independent monitoring, according to the assessment's implementation considerations.
CAB Secretary General Advocate Humayun Kabir Bhuiyan chaired the dialogue, while CAB research coordinator Shuvo Kibria moderated it.

item.title: Faqir Mahbub: Attempt underway to add 300MW from Rooppur plant to national grid by Nov
item.description:
Postal, Telecommunications and Information Technology, and Science and Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam on Thursday said efforts are underway to supply around 300 megawatts (MW) of electricity from the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant to the national grid by November.
"We are making all-out efforts to supply nearly 300MW of electricity from the first reactor of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant to the national grid by this coming November. In addition, we plan to load nuclear fuel into the second reactor around June next year," said the minister.
Underlining the priority attached to the project, Minister Anam noted that as the 1,200MW capacity mega project is a flagship initiative of Russia's state atomic energy corporation, Rosatom, the Russian side is giving it top priority. Teams of experts sent three months ago are working round the clock to meet the project targets.
During his interaction, the minister also addressed recent queries regarding the mobile financial service provider "Nagad". Clarifying the government’s stance, he stated that the government has no plan or intention to sell Nagad.
He highlighted that Nagad is currently operating in a profitable state and assured that steps will be taken to make the platform even more modern and profitable in the future.

item.title: Titumir: IMF, development partners to support Bangladesh's reform priorities
item.description:
Prime Minister's Adviser on Finance and Planning Prof Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir on Thursday said that the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the World Bank and other development partners will support Bangladesh's reform programs in line with the country's own priorities and strategies.
"For the first time, international development partners are clearly expressing their willingness to support reform initiatives based on Bangladesh's priorities," he said, adding that this would create scope for the country to pursue reforms in line with its own plans.
The adviser made the remarks while briefing journalists on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the IMF and the World Bank in Bangkok.
Titumir said that, besides the IMF and the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) and relevant agencies of China and the United States were also extending cooperation in implementing reforms based on Bangladesh's priorities.
Asked whether conditions attached to IMF loans could pose an obstacle, he said the issues would proceed through the established process. The government was working to implement each step quickly and effectively, and remained optimistic about taking effective measures in this regard.
On the IMF's economic growth and inflation forecasts, the adviser said the projections should also be viewed in terms of the potential impact on the economy if the planned reforms were not implemented.
He said differences among forecasts by international organizations were normal, adding that a review of past data suggested that the IMF's growth projections were generally somewhat conservative.
Referring to the IMF's Article IV mission report, Titumir said Bangladesh's growth forecast had been put at 4.7%. However, the government remained optimistic about achieving its budgetary growth target of 6.5%.
He said the reform agenda had been incorporated into the government's election manifesto and would also be reflected in the forthcoming five-year economic strategy.
The government believed that implementing the planned reforms would strengthen the economy's capacity.capacit, he added.
On inflation, Titumir said several factors were contributing to the persistent pressure on prices, including developments in the Middle East and long-standing inflationary pressures inherited from the past.
Reducing the cost of living for ordinary people and protecting vulnerable households remained key government priorities, he added.
The adviser acknowledged weaknesses in the previous social protection system, saying beneficiary selection had often been flawed.
"Many deserving people had been excluded, while others who were not entitled to benefits had been included. Fragmented implementation had also prevented the programmes from delivering their expected results," he added.
Citing a World Bank report, he said deficiencies in effective social protection over recent years had contributed to rising poverty.
To address the situation, he said, the government was pursuing initiatives such as the Family Card and Farmers Card to improve beneficiary selection through scientific methods and ensure that assistance reached the intended recipients.
He said the government was also emphasizing the development of digital public infrastructure to make social protection programs more effective.
Development partners had responded positively to the government's target of allocating five percent of GDP to the social sector and its plan to increase health spending, he said, adding that cooperation to support these priorities had also been discussed.
Titumir said the government aimed to raise tax collection to 10% of GDP by 2030. Restoring discipline in the banking sector, protecting depositors' interests and ensuring accountability across the financial sector were also major priorities.
He said the government had taken initiatives to return deposits to customers of Sammilito Islami Bank to ensure the security of depositors' money.
Measures would also be taken to improve transparency in banks' financial statements and balance sheets and reform the necessary legal frameworks, he added.
Highlighting past financial irregularities, Titumir said common people were bearing a heavy cost due to the plundering of funds from banks and other sectors.
According to him, around $40 billion had been looted from the banking sector.
He stressed that the money belonged to the people and those involved in financial irregularities and plundering must be held accountable.
He said both those who had siphoned off money and those who had facilitated such activities must face accountability, regardless of whether they were in Bangladesh or abroad.
A coordinated effort was needed to tackle defaulted loans and financial irregularities, he said, adding that holding those who assisted financial offenders accountable would help discourage similar crimes in the future.
The IMF and World Bank Group annual meetings are being held in Bangkok, Thailand, from October 12 to Sunday. The meetings are discussing a range of issues, including the global economic outlook, financial stability, poverty reduction and inclusive growth.

item.title: Saudi coalition says missile intercepted in Medina region
item.description:
The Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis on Thursday said it had intercepted a cruise missile in the Medina region -- home to one of Islam’s holiest cities, but the Houthis denied carrying out any such attack.
“Interception and destruction of a cruise missile in the Medina region,” coalition spokesman Turki Al-Malki wrote on X, with the statement also published by state media.
The Houthis quickly responded by saying they did not target the region on Thursday, and had previously vowed to spare the holy cities of Medina and Mecca.
Saudi Arabia has in recent days come under sustained attack from the Houthis, including a strike on Riyadh’s international airport that was the kingdom’s deadliest in years, as the war with the group escalates.
Riyadh has hit back with strikes against the Iran-backed group’s stronghold in the Yemeni capital Sanaa.
Medina, the burial place of the Prophet Mohammed and home to the Prophet’s Mosque, is one of Islam’s holiest cities alongside Mecca.
The Houthis have vowed to continue targeting airports and other sites across Saudi Arabia but on Sunday said Mecca and Medina would be spared.
“The Yemeni armed forces confirm that they have not carried out any operation today targeting Saudi territory, and that the Saudi enemy’s claims of an attack on Medina are a shameless and brazen lie,” Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree wrote on X on Thursday.
On Wednesday the Houthis said they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco, with Saudi officials reporting a strike on a building in an area housing the energy giant’s operations center.
The Saudi-led coalition has supported Yemen’s government militarily against the Houthis since 2015 in a long-running civil war that has created a humanitarian crisis.

The Cabinet Division has issued a notification in this regard recently.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has been made the convener of the committee, while the civil aviation and tourism minister, chief of air staff, home secretary, principal staff officer of the Armed Forces Division, civil aviation and tourism secretary, and inspector general of police have been named as members.

item.title: NBR extends VAT return submission deadline to October 25
item.description:
The National Board of Revenue (NBR) has extended the deadline for submitting online VAT returns for the three tax periods from July to September in its e-VAT system.
Taxpayers can now file these returns without any interest or penalties until October 25.
This decision was announced in a notification issued on Thursday (October 15), signed by Sheikh Md Masudur Rahman, second secretary of the NBR (VAT: Monitoring, Statistics, and Coordination).
The notification stated that following amendments to the VAT return submission regulations at the end of every three tax periods in the National Budget 2026–27, the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026 was promulgated.
As a result of incorporating the provision to submit VAT returns after each three-tax-period cycle, certain administrative reforms were required within the e-VAT system.
In this context, in the public interest, the NBR—exercising powers granted under Sub-section (2) of Section 64 of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012—has extended the deadline for submitting online returns for the July–September 2026 tax periods without interest or penalty until October 25.
Meanwhile, the government has issued a new ordinance establishing deadlines for submitting Value Added Tax (VAT) returns.
Under the new provisions, standard registered, enlisted, registrable, or enlistable entities must submit their returns within 15 days following the end of a tax period.
However, government, semi-government, and autonomous organizations, banks, insurance companies, and entities filing nil-returns will have up to 20 days to submit their returns.
The "Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026" was officially published in an extra edition of the Bangladesh Gazette on October 14.

item.title: Govt borrows Tk24,245cr from banks in Q1 of FY27
item.description:
The government tapped the banking sector for Tk24,245 crore during the first quarter of FY27, underscoring its expanding reliance on bank credit amidst sluggish tax revenues.
This net borrowing throughout the July–September period represents a stark shift from the Tk6,926 crore in net debt repayments made over the same period in FY26, based on Bangladesh Bank figures.
During these three months, public borrowing comprised Tk1,017 crore drawn directly from the central bank alongside Tk23,227 crore secured from commercial lenders.
In FY26, total government bank borrowing reached Tk131,000 crore, eclipsing its official annual target of Tk104,000 crore and rising sharply above the Tk72,372 crore borrowed in FY25.
For FY27, official plans set the bank borrowing threshold at Tk112,000 crore.
Cumulative public debt owed to the domestic banking system crossed the Tk700,000 crore mark as of September 30.
The accelerating credit uptake reflects a persistent shortfall between state revenue generation and spending commitments.
Authorities depend heavily on bank loans to fund infrastructure projects, welfare initiatives, public sector payrolls, and operational expenses, as revenue generation continues to lag behind outlay requirements.
Bangladesh Bank’s monetary policy statement covering July–December 2026 highlighted that government financing shifted heavily toward commercial lenders after the central bank halted automated debt creation (devolvement), while intake through National Savings Certificates also rebounded.
This mounting reliance on commercial banks raises concerns regarding the government's capacity to fund operations without squeezing out credit to private enterprises.
Commercial financial institutions may favor allocating capital to government treasury bills and bonds—which carry minimal default risk—rather than extending credit to businesses in an environment of elevated default risks and broader economic uncertainty.
Private sector credit growth slowed to a mere 4.7% in August 2026, indicating subdued corporate investment appetite alongside constraints on lenders' balance sheet capacity.
Additional crowding-out pressure from public borrowing threatens to restrict capital available for corporate expansion, industrial output, and job creation, potentially dampening overall economic recovery.
However, the liquidity impact remains uneven across the sector.
Institutions holding surplus liquidity can readily expand their government securities portfolios, whereas distressed lenders continue to struggle under severe liquidity constraints.
Consequently, state borrowing needs risk escalating interbank competition for deposits across an already fragile banking industry.
Direct borrowing from Bangladesh Bank carries distinct inflationary risks whenever it expands the monetary base and total money supply without generating a corresponding increase in real economic output.
While borrowing from commercial banks does not exert the same immediate expansionary impact on money supply, it directly crowds out private sector borrowers.
Strains on public finances could escalate further if international fuel and commodity import costs jump due to conflict in the Middle East, driving up state subsidies and borrowing requirements.
Curtailing this structural dependence will necessitate aggressive revenue mobilization, modernized tax administration, and stricter fiscal discipline over public expenditure, according to independent economists.

item.title: National Bank starts repaying its depositors
item.description:
National Bank restarted routine banking operations on Thursday, enabling general depositors to withdraw cash according to their requirements.
The bank began processing deposit payouts for clients who submitted withdrawal requests over the preceding four days.
According to sources within National Bank, the distressed lender secured Tk7,000 crore in liquidity support to resume regular functions. State-run Sonali Bank provided these funds backed by a central bank guarantee.
Bangladesh Bank has applied strict guidelines regarding how National Bank may deploy the capital.
A primary stipulation prohibits using these funds to settle deposits belonging to present or former bank directors, nor can the money be disbursed as loans.
The central bank outlined these directives in a official communication sent to National Bank’s managing director on Monday.
The notice specified that the liquidity assistance carries a 10% interest rate with a maturity period of three months.
In the interim, the lender gathered cash withdrawal requests from clients between October 11 and 14 to gauge overall liquidity demand.
National Bank sources indicated that roughly 11,000 customers applied to withdraw a combined total of Tk2,000 crore across those four days.
Branches nationwide submitted their depositors' requests to the head office, which subsequently supplied the necessary cash.
As an initial measure, the bank was directed to clear withdrawal requests from savings and current account holders over the coming days, with other client categories receiving payouts in later phases.
11 conditions
National Bank must adhere to 11 central bank conditions governing the usage of these funds raised under the central bank guarantee to satisfy depositor claims.
Among these rules, the bank cannot declare cash dividends until the assistance package is fully repaid.
Furthermore, the money cannot be channeled toward loans or investments for current or former directors, or any entities connected to them.
The capital must not be used to refund deposits registered to past or present directors—whether directly or via indirect channels—nor can it back new credit approvals or increase existing credit facilities.
Even previously sanctioned but undisbursed loan amounts cannot be released using this liquidity.
Bangladesh Bank additionally barred using the capital to settle existing interbank obligations or placements, buy out loans or investment portfolios from peer banks, or purchase foreign currency to meet letter of credit obligations linked to forced loans or loans against trust receipts (LTRs).
Depositing the funds into other financial institutions is likewise forbidden.
For the duration of the guarantee, all newly mobilized deposits must be allocated exclusively toward improving the bank's overall liquidity and fulfilling commitments to general depositors.
Operating costs cannot grow by more than 5% year-over-year, and the guaranteed capital cannot be applied toward administrative or operational expenditures.
National Bank is required to submit weekly usage reports to the central bank detailing how the funds are deployed.
Data from National Bank indicates that as of October 12, total deposits stood at Tk33,515 crore, while outstanding loans reached Tk43,230 crore. This resulted in an advance-to-deposit ratio (ADR) of 132%.
Under Bangladesh Bank regulations, commercial banks may lend up to Tk87 for every Tk100 in deposits, placing the maximum allowable ADR ceiling at 87%. By the end of June, nearly 66% of National Bank’s total loan portfolio was classified as non-performing loans.
Latest accounting figures reveal that National Bank’s cumulative borrowings from Bangladesh Bank and other financial institutions—including funds secured through central bank guarantees—total approximately Tk26,000 crore.
Sikder Group held management control over National Bank from 2009 through 2023. Extensive financial irregularities during this timeframe caused substantial losses, pushing the institution into acute financial distress.
